title: ZeroGR: A Generalizable and Scalable Framework for Zero-Shot Generative Retrieval
abstract:
Generative retrieval (GR) reformulates information retrieval (IR) by framing it as the generation of document identifiers (docids), thereby enabling an end-to-end optimization and seamless integration with generative language models (LMs).
Despite notable progress under supervised training, GR still struggles to generalize to zero-shot IR scenarios, which are prevalent in real-world applications. 
To tackle this challenge, we propose ZeroGR, a zero-shot generative retrieval framework that leverages natural language instructions to extend GR across a wide range of IR tasks.
Specifically, ZeroGR is composed of three key components: (i) an LM-based docid generator that unifies heterogeneous documents (e.g., text, tables, code) into  semantically meaningful docids; (ii) an instruction-tuned query generator that generates diverse types of queries from natural language task descriptions to enhance corpus indexing; and (iii) a reverse annealing decoding strategy to balance precision and recall during docid generation. 
We investigate the impact of instruction fine-tuning scale and find that performance consistently improves as the number of IR tasks encountered during training increases.
Empirical results on the BEIR and MAIR benchmarks demonstrate that \textsc{ZeroGR} outperforms strong dense retrieval and generative baselines in zero-shot settings, establishing a new state-of-the-art for instruction-driven GR.
problem: Generative retrieval struggles to generalize to zero-shot IR scenarios prevalent in real-world applications despite progress under supervised training.
approach: ZeroGR leverages natural language instructions to extend generative retrieval across IR tasks, using LM-based docid generation, instruction-tuned query generation, and reverse annealing decoding.
contribution: ZeroGR outperforms dense retrieval and generative baselines on BEIR and MAIR zero-shot benchmarks, establishing state-of-the-art for instruction-driven generative retrieval.
